Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 1:

Name of the Surah

• It is called Ali 'Imran (The Family of 'Imran), because it mentions the family of 'Imran, their virtues and their accounts, the affair of Maryam (Mary) and her son, peace be upon him, and the manifestations of divine power that appeared at his birth.

Objectives of the Surah

• Praising the Qur'an and affirming that it is the truth, establishing its truthfulness and the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ), extolling the virtue of Islam and that no religion other than it is accepted by Allah, and refuting the doubts raised against the Qur'an, Islam, and the Messenger (ﷺ) by the People of the Book.

• Affirming the existence of Allah and His oneness in divinity, mentioning the proofs for that, clarifying the misguidance of those who take deities besides Allah, and warning the polytheists that their affair is heading toward extinction.

• Discussing the Christians of Najran, who disputed with the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, and denied the message of the Prophet (ﷺ); and the decisive refutation, with clear proofs, of the claims and beliefs of the Christians; and debating the People of the Two Scriptures regarding the reality of hanifiyyah (pure monotheism), and that they are far from it; and exposing the errors and fabrications of the Jews in their religion, and their concealment of what was revealed to them.

• Reminding the Muslims of Allah's blessing upon them through this religion, reminding them of their previous state in the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance), guiding them to patience and perseverance in the cause of the religion, and promising them victory and support for that.

• Discussing hypocrisy and the hypocrites, and their stance in discouraging the determination of the believers, and warning against their scheming and malice.

• Discussing the Battle of Uhud and the Battle of Badr, and the lessons the Muslims learned from these two expeditions.

• Mentioning a number of legal rulings, such as Hajj, jihad, and the prohibition of riba (usury), and commanding the Muslims to virtuous deeds, such as spending wealth to aid the Ummah and to do good, and abandoning stinginess.

• Guiding people to reflect on the dominion of Allah, in the heavens and the earth, and the two signs of night and day, and what is in that of wonders, secrets, innovation and perfection, which point to the existence of the Wise Creator.

[Tafsir]

﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ Its discussion has already preceded at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.
He is Allah; there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the One who possesses perfect life as befits His majesty, the One who sustains and watches over everything.

He sent down to you, O Messenger, the Qur'an with the truth, which contains no doubt, confirming what came before it of scriptures and messengers. He had sent down the Torah to Musa (peace be upon him) and the Injil to Isa (peace be upon him) before the revelation of the Qur'an, as guidance for the God-fearing toward faith, and for the righteousness of their religion and their worldly life. And He sent down that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood. As for those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah that were sent down, they will have a severe punishment. Allah is All-Mighty, none can overcome Him, and He is Owner of retribution against those who deny His proofs and evidences, and His sole divinity.

He had sent down the Torah to Musa (peace be upon him) and the Injil to Isa (peace be upon him) before the revelation of the Qur'an, as guidance for the God-fearing toward faith, and for the righteousness of their religion and their worldly life. And He sent down that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood. As for those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah that were sent down, they will have a severe punishment. This passage is from the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar), on Surah 3, verse 5.

"Indeed, Allah's knowledge encompasses all of creation. Nothing on the earth or in the heavens is hidden from Him, whether it is small or great."

It is He alone who forms you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills: male or female, beautiful or ugly, wretched or happy. There is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the All-Mighty who cannot be overpowered, the All-Wise in His command and His arrangement.

He it is Who has sent down to you the Book: in it are verses that are clear in meaning (muhkamat), which are the foundation of the Book, to which one refers when there is ambiguity, and whatever contradicts them is returned to them. And in it are other verses that are allegorical (mutashabihat), which admit of some meanings, and their intended meaning is not determined except by joining them to the clear verses. As for those whose hearts are diseased and deviant, due to their bad intent, they follow only these allegorical verses, in order to stir up doubts among people, so that they may lead them astray, and for their interpreting them according to their false doctrines. And none knows the reality of these allegorical verses and what they will ultimately come to mean except God. And those firmly grounded in knowledge say: "We believe in this Qur'an; all of it has come to us from our Lord through His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ)," and they refer its allegorical verses back to its clear verses. Only those of sound intellect understand, reflect upon and comprehend the meanings in their correct form.

And they say: "Our Lord, do not let our hearts swerve from belief in You after You have guided us to Your religion, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower: abundant in favour and giving, You give to whomever You will without measure."

This is a short tafsir passage (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, King Fahd Complex) on Surah Al-Imran, verse 9. Here is the translation:

"O our Lord, indeed we acknowledge and testify that You will gather the people on a Day about which there is no doubt, and that is the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break Your promise to Your servants."

Indeed, those who rejected the true religion and denied it, their wealth and their children will not avail them anything against the punishment of Allah if it befalls them in this world, nor will they ward it off from them in the Hereafter. These are the fuel of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

The condition of the disbelievers in their denial and what befalls them is like the condition of the people of Pharaoh and those before them among the disbelievers. They denied the clear signs of Allah, so He seized them with punishment because of their denial and obstinacy. And Allah is severe in punishment toward whoever disbelieves in Him and denies His messengers.

Say, [O Messenger], to those who disbelieve, [among] the Jews and others, and to those who held in contempt Your victory at Badr: "You will be defeated in this world, and you will die upon disbelief, and you will be gathered into the Fire of Hell, to be for you a constant bed, and wretched is the bed."

Verily there has been for you, O Jews, arrogant and obstinate, a great sign in the two groups that met in the battle of Badr: one group fighting for the religion of God, namely Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions, and another group, disbelieving in God, fighting for falsehood. You saw the believers in number as twice their own number with your own eyes, and God made that a cause of the victory of the Muslims over them. God strengthens with His help whomever He wills of His servants. Indeed, in what happened there is a great admonition for people of insight, who are guided to the judgment of God and His actions.

Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, sons, heaped-up wealth of gold and silver, fine horses, livestock of camels, cattle and sheep, and cultivated land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and its perishable adornment. With Allah is the excellent return and reward, and it is Paradise.

Say, [O Messenger]: Shall I inform you of something better than what has been made attractive to people in this worldly life? For those who fear God and dread His punishment, there are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and for them therein are spouses purified from menstruation and postpartum bleeding, and from bad character. And for them there is something greater than that: the good pleasure of God. God is Ever-Seeing of His servants' inner secrets, Knowing of their conditions, and He will recompense them for that.
These righteous servants say: "Indeed, we have believed in You and followed Your Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so erase from us the sins we have committed, and save us from the punishment of the Fire."

They are the ones who have the qualities of patience in obeying God, patience in refraining from sins, and patience in bearing the painful decrees of God that befall them; who are truthful in their words and deeds; who are completely obedient; who spend in charity, both secretly and openly; and who seek forgiveness in the last part of the night, because it is the time most likely for acceptance and the answering of supplication.

Allah bears witness that He alone is the one deserving worship, and He joined His witness with the witness of the angels and the people of knowledge, concerning the most glorious matter to be witnessed to: His oneness, exalted is He, and His upholding of justice. There is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the Almighty (al-'Azīz) over whom nothing He wills can be prevented, the All-Wise (al-Ḥakīm) in His sayings and His actions.

Indeed, the religion acceptable to Allah for His creation, with which He sent His messengers, and which He does not accept from anyone other than it, is Islam (islām), which is submission to Allah alone in obedience and surrender to Him in worship, and following the messengers in what Allah sent them with in every era, until they were sealed by Muhammad (ﷺ), after whose mission Allah does not accept from anyone any religion other than Islam with which he was sent. The disagreement among the People of the Scripture, the Jews and the Christians, which led them to split into sects and factions, occurred only after the proof had been established against them through the sending of messengers and the revelation of books; (it was born of) insolence, envy, and the pursuit of worldly gain. As for whoever denies the signs of Allah that were revealed, and His signs that point to His lordship and divinity, then indeed Allah is swift in reckoning, and He will recompense them for what they used to do.

If they dispute with you, O Messenger, concerning monotheism after you have established the proof against them, then say to them: "I have devoted myself entirely to God alone, and I do not associate anyone with Him." And likewise, those believers who follow me should devote themselves to God and submit to Him. Say to them, and to the idolaters of the Arabs and others: "If you submit, then you are upon the straight path, the guidance and the truth. But if you turn away, then your reckoning is with God, and my duty is only to convey the message, and I have conveyed it to you and established the proof against you." And God is Seeing of His servants; nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 21:

Indeed, those who deny the clear signs and what the messengers brought, and who kill the prophets of Allah unjustly, without any right, and who kill those who enjoin justice and follow the path of the prophets, so give them the good news of a painful punishment.

Those are the ones whose deeds have been nullified in this world and in the Hereafter. So no deed of theirs will be accepted, and they will have no helper to protect them from the punishment of Allah.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the strange state of these Jews, who were given a portion of the Book and yet know that what you have brought is the truth? They are called to the Book of Allah, which is the Qur'an, so that it may judge between them concerning what they disagree about. But when it does not agree with their desires, many of them refuse the judgment of Allah, because it is their habit to turn away from the truth?

That turning away from the truth is caused by a corrupt belief held by the People of the Book: that they will be punished only for a few days. This belief led them to become bold against Allah and to make light of His religion, and to persist in their false religion, by which they deceived themselves.

How will it be with them when Allah gathers them to be called to account on a Day about which there is no doubt, which is the Day of Resurrection, and every soul is given in full what it has earned, while they will not be wronged in anything?

Say, [O Prophet], addressing your Lord in supplication: "O You who possess all sovereignty! You grant sovereignty, wealth, and establishment on earth to whomever You will of Your creation, and You strip sovereignty from whomever You will. You bestow honour in this world and the Hereafter upon whomever You will, and You place humiliation upon whomever You will. In Your hand is all good, and You alone are over all things Competent." And in the verse there is an affirmation of the attribute of the Hand for Allah, Exalted is He, in a manner befitting Him.

Among the signs of Your power is that You cause the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night, so this lengthens and that shortens. You bring the living out of the dead, that which has no life in it, like bringing the plant out of the seed, and the believer out of the disbeliever. You bring the dead out of the living, like bringing the egg out of the hen. And You provide sustenance to whomever You will of Your creation without reckoning.

God forbids the believers from taking the disbelievers as allies, giving them love and support in preference to the believers. Whoever allies himself with them has then severed himself from God, and God has severed Himself from him, except where you are weak and fearful: then God has permitted you to make a truce with them in order to protect yourselves from their evil, until your strength grows. God warns you of Himself, so fear Him and be wary of Him. And to God alone is the return of all creatures, for reckoning and recompense.

Say, O Prophet, to the believers: whether you conceal what is settled in your hearts of allegiance to the disbelievers and supporting them, or you reveal it, nothing of it is hidden from Allah. Indeed, His knowledge encompasses everything in the heavens and everything on the earth, and He has complete power over everything.

On the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Recompense, every soul will find whatever good it did waiting for it in full, so that it may be rewarded for it. And whatever evil deed it did, it will find that too awaiting it, and it will wish that there were a long distance of time between it and that deed. So prepare yourselves for this Day, and fear the assault of the Mighty God. Yet despite the severity of His punishment, He, glorified be He, is characterized by perfect mercy toward His servants.

Say, [O Messenger]: If you truly love Allah, then follow me, and believe in me outwardly and inwardly; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. For He is Forgiving toward the sins of His believing servants and Merciful to them. This noble verse is a judge over everyone who claims to love Allah, the Exalted, while not truly following His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and obeying him in his commands and prohibitions. Such a person is a liar in his claim until he follows the Messenger (ﷺ) in the true sense of following.

Say, O Messenger: Obey God by following His Book, and obey the Messenger by following his Sunnah (the Prophetic way and teachings) both during his lifetime and after his death. But if they turn away from you and persist in the disbelief and misguidance they are upon, then they are not deserving of God's love, for God does not love the disbelievers.
Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran, and made them superior to the people of their times.

These prophets and messengers are a continuous chain of purity in sincerity to Allah, in His Oneness, and in acting upon His revelation. And Allah is All-Hearing of His servants' words, All-Knowing of their deeds, and He will recompense them for that.

Mention, O Messenger, the matter of Maryam, her mother, and her son ʿIsa (peace be upon him), so that by this you may refute those who claimed that ʿIsa was divine or the son of Allah, subhanahu. When the wife of ʿImran said, upon becoming pregnant: "My Lord, I have dedicated to You what is in my womb, purely for Your service, to serve the Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy Sanctuary). So accept it from me. Indeed, You alone are the All-Hearing of my supplication, the All-Knowing of my intention."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 36:

When her term was complete and she had given birth to her child, she said: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," — and Allah knew best what she had given birth to, and He will make her a matter of great significance — "and the male is not like the female," [she said,] "for the male is stronger for service and more capable of it. I have named her Maryam, and I place her and her offspring under Your protection from Satan, the accursed, who is driven away from Your mercy."

Then Allah accepted her supplication and received her vow in the best manner of acceptance, and He placed her daughter Maryam under His care, so He made her grow in a goodly growth. And Allah made it easy for Zakariyya, peace be upon him, to become her guardian (kafil). So he housed her in the place of His worship, and whenever he entered upon her in this place, he found with her provision, ready and wholesome. He said: "O Maryam, from where is this good provision for you?" She said: "It is provision from the presence of Allah. Indeed Allah, by His bounty, provides whomever He wills of His creation without reckoning."

When Zakariyya saw what Allah had honoured Maryam with of His provision and bounty, he turned to his Lord, saying: "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good and blessed offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication to whoever calls upon You."

Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary before Allah: "Indeed, Allah gives you good news that will gladden you: you will be granted a son named Yahya (John). He will confirm a word from Allah, namely ʿIsa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him). Yahya will be a sayyid (chief, leader) among his people, possessing high standing and rank, and a ḥaṣūr (one who keeps himself chaste), who does not commit sins or indulge in harmful desires. He will be a prophet from among the righteous, who have reached the utmost peak of righteousness."

Zechariah said, joyful and amazed: "My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has already reached its utmost in me, and my wife is barren and cannot bear children?" He said: "Thus does God do what He wills, performing wondrous deeds that run contrary to the usual course of things."

Zakariyya said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign by which I may know that a child has come to me, so that joy and good tidings may be mine." He said: "Your sign is that you will not be able to speak to the people for three days except by gesture, though you are sound and healthy. During this period, remember your Lord often and glorify Him at the end of the day and at its beginning."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 42:

Remember, O Messenger, when the angels said: "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you for His obedience, and purified you from base character, and chosen you above the women of the worlds in your time."

O Mary, devote yourself constantly to obedience to your Lord, stand in humble submission, prostrate yourself, and bow down along with those who bow; in gratitude to God for the blessings He has bestowed upon you.

That which We have related to you, O Messenger, of the news of the unseen, which Allah has revealed to you, is because you were not with them when they disputed over who would be entrusted with the care of Maryam, who among them was more deserving and more entitled to her. A dispute arose among them, so they cast lots by throwing their pens, and the lot fell upon Zakariyya, peace be upon him, and he won her guardianship.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 45:

You, O Prophet of Allah, were not there when the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary. He will be distinguished in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be one of those brought near [to Allah]." That is, He says to him, "Be," and he is. His name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; he has great honor in this world and the Hereafter, and he is among those brought near to Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Speaking to people while still in the cradle, before the age of speech, and calling them to God when he is grown, his strength gathered and his youth complete, with what God revealed to him. This is the speech of prophethood, of da'wah (calling to God) and of guidance, and he is counted among the people of righteousness and virtue in his words and his deeds.

Maryam said, astonished at this matter: "How can I have a son when no man has touched me and I am not unchaste?" The angel said to her: "This which is happening to you is not far-fetched for the All-Powerful God, who brings into existence whatever He wills from nothing. When He wills to bring something into being, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is."
And He will teach him writing, and rightness in speech and action, and the Tawrat (Torah) that Allah revealed to Musa, peace be upon him, and the Injil (Gospel) that Allah sent down to him.

And He will make him a messenger to the Children of Israel, and he will say to them: "Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, showing that I am a messenger sent from God. It is this: I will fashion for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then I will breathe into it, and it will become a real bird by God's permission. I will also heal the one born blind and the one afflicted with leprosy (baras), and I will bring the dead to life by God's permission, and I will inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses of your food. Indeed, in these great matters, which are beyond the power of human beings, is a clear proof that I am the Prophet of God and His messenger, if you are truthful in affirming the proofs and signs of God and acknowledging His oneness."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 50:

"I have come to you confirming what is before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what Allah had forbidden to you, as a lightening (of the burden) and a mercy from Allah. And I have come to you with a proof from your Lord for the truth of what I say to you. So fear Allah and do not oppose His command, and obey me in what I convey to you from Allah."
Indeed, Allah, the One to whom I call you, alone is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. I and you are equal in servitude and submission to Him, and this is the path with no crookedness in it.

When Jesus sensed their determination to disbelieve, he called out to his chosen companions: "Who will be my helpers in the cause of God's religion?" The disciples of Jesus replied: "We are the helpers of God's religion and those who call to it. We have believed in God and followed you. And you, O Jesus, bear witness that we have submitted to God in monotheism and obedience."

Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed of the Injil (Gospel), and we have followed Your Messenger, Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him. So make us among those who bear witness for You to (Your) oneness and for Your prophets to (their) message, and they are the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), who bear witness for the Messengers that they conveyed (the message) to their nations.

The plotting of those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved against ʿĪsā (ʿalayhi al-salām): they commissioned someone to kill him by stealth. But Allah cast the likeness of ʿĪsā upon a man who had pointed them to him, so they seized him, killed him and crucified him, thinking that he was ʿĪsā (ʿalayhi al-salām). ﴿And Allah is the best of planners.﴾ In this there is an affirmation of the attribute of planning (makr) for Allah, Exalted is He, in a manner befitting His majesty and perfection, for it is planning in truth, in response to the planning of the planners.

And Allah plotted against them, and Allah is the best of plotters, when Allah said to Jesus: "I will take you (mutawaffika) from the earth without any harm reaching you, and raise you up to Me with your body and your soul, and purify you from those who disbelieve in you. And I will make those who follow you superior over those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me will be your return, all of you, on the Day of Reckoning, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ regarding the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him."

Note on the sentence above: "and Allah is the best of plotters" is part of the verse itself and is rendered from ﴿وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾ only as it appears in the commentary; the commentary text provided begins with "ومكر الله بهم," so the added clause is not in the source passage and should be removed.

Corrected translation of the passage as given:

And Allah plotted against them when Allah said to Jesus: "I will take you from the earth without any harm reaching you, and raise you up to Me with your body and your soul, and purify you from those who disbelieve in you. And I will make those who follow you superior over those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me will be your return, all of you, on the Day of Reckoning, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ regarding the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 56:

As for those who disbelieved in the Messiah from among the Jews, or who exaggerated concerning him from among the Christians, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world, by killing, the seizing of their wealth, and the removal of their dominion; and in the Hereafter, with the Fire. And they will have no helper who could help them or ward off the punishment of Allah from them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 57:

As for those who believed in Allah and His messengers and did righteous deeds, Allah will give them the full reward of their deeds, without any diminution. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers, [those who commit wrong] through polytheism (shirk) and disbelief (kufr).

That which We recite to you concerning Jesus is among the clear proofs of the truth of your message and of the truth of the Wise Qur'an, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, so there is no doubt or disputation concerning it.

The creation of Jesus by God without a father is like the creation of Adam by God without a father or a mother. For He created him from the dust of the earth, then said to him, "Be a human being," and he was. So the claim that Jesus is divine because he was created without a father is a false claim, for Adam, peace be upon him, was created without a father or a mother, and everyone agrees that he was a servant among the servants of God.

The truth that is beyond doubt concerning the matter of Jesus is that which has come to you, O Messenger, from your Lord. So remain steadfast in your certainty, and in your state of refraining from fabrication, and do not be among those who doubt. In this there is reassurance and comfort for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 61:

Whoever disputes with you, [O Messenger], concerning Jesus, the son of Mary, after the knowledge has come to you about the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him), say to them: "Come, let us summon our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves. Then let us turn to Allah in supplication, asking that He send down His punishment and curse upon the liars in their claim, those who persist in their obstinacy."

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 3, verse 62:

Indeed, this that I have told you, O Messenger, about the matter of Jesus is the true report, about which there is no doubt. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, and indeed Allah is the Mighty in His dominion, the Wise in His management and His actions.
If they turn away from believing you and following you, then they are the corruptors, and Allah is All-Knowing of them, and He will recompense them for that.

Say, [O Messenger], to the People of the Scripture, Jews and Christians: "Come to a word that is just and true, on which we all agree: that we single out Allah alone for worship, associate nothing with Him, whether an idol, a statue, a cross, a tyrant (ṭāghūt), or anything else, and that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah by obeying them in ways that Allah has not commanded." If they turn away from this good call, then say to them, [O believers]: "Bear witness that we are Muslims, submitting to our Lord in servitude and sincere devotion."

The call to a common word, as it is addressed to the Jews and Christians, is likewise addressed to whoever follows their path.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 65:

O People of the Scripture, from the Jews and the Christians, why do you dispute, each of you, concerning Abraham (peace be upon him), claiming that he was upon your religion, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Do you not understand the error of your statement that Abraham was a Jew or a Christian, when you know that Judaism and Christianity came into being long after his death?

Here you are, O people, you argued with the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (ﷺ), about matters of your religion of which you have knowledge, those things you believe to be true in your books. So why do you argue about matters of which you have no knowledge concerning Abraham? And Allah knows matters in their hidden depths, while you do not know.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 67:

Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian. Judaism and Christianity did not appear until after him. Rather, he was one who followed the command of Allah and obeyed Him, submitting to his Lord, and he was not among the polytheists.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 68:

Indeed, the people most entitled to Ibrahim (Abraham) and closest to him are those who believed in him, affirmed his message, and followed him in his religion. And this Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ), and those who believe in him [are such]. And Allah is the Guardian (walī) of the believers who believe in Him and follow His law (sharīʿah).

A group of the Jews and Christians wished that they could lead you astray, O Muslims, away from Islam. But they lead astray only themselves and their followers, and they do not realize this or perceive it.

O People of the Torah and the Gospel, why do you deny the signs of Allah that He sent down to His messengers in your scriptures, in which is (the statement) that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the awaited Messenger, and that what has come to you from him is the truth, while you yourselves bear witness to that? Yet you deny it.

O People of the Scripture (the Torah and the Gospel), why do you mix the truth with falsehood, distorting and writing with your own hands what is false, and concealing what is in your scriptures about the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and that his religion is the truth, while you know this?

A group of the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) from the Jews said: "Believe in what has been sent down to those who believed at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, so that perhaps they will doubt their religion and turn away from it."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 73:

And do not believe with true belief except those who follow your religion (i.e., the Jews). Say to them, O Messenger: "Indeed, the guidance and success are the guidance of Allah and His granting of success to sound faith." And they said: "Do not reveal what you have of knowledge to the Muslims, lest they learn it from you and become equal to you in knowledge of it, and they would have superiority over you, or lest they use it as an argument before your Lord by which they overcome you." Say to them, O Messenger: "Indeed, bounty, giving, and all matters are in the hand of Allah and under His control. He gives them to whomever He wills of those who believe in Him and His Messenger. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing," encompassing by His knowledge and His giving all His creatures, among those who deserve His bounty and favors.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, the "Simplified Tafsir") on surah 3, verse 74:

Indeed, Allah singles out for His mercy from among His creation whomever He wills, with prophethood and guidance to the most complete laws (sharai'). And Allah is the Lord of kindness, of abundant and far-reaching giving.

Among the People of the Scripture are some who, if you entrust them with a large amount of wealth, will return it to you without betrayal; and among them are some who, if you entrust them with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you exert the utmost effort in demanding it. The cause of this is a corrupt belief that makes them consider the wealth of the Arabs permissible to take unjustly, and they say: "There is no blame or sin upon us in consuming their wealth, for Allah has made it lawful for us." This is a lie against Allah, which they utter with their tongues while they know that they are liars.

It is not as these liars claim. Rather, the truly God-fearing person (al-muttaqi) is the one who fulfills what he pledged to God: discharging trusts, believing in Him and in His messengers, and adhering to His guidance and law. He fears God, the Mighty and Majestic, so he complies with His command and refrains from what He has forbidden. Indeed, God loves the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), those who guard themselves against shirk (associating partners with God) and sins.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 77:

Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and His charge, which He enjoined in the Scriptures He sent down to their prophets, for a base and paltry price, from the goods and fleeting trappings of this world, those will have no share of reward in the Hereafter. Allah will not speak to them in a way that would gladden them, nor will He look upon them on the Day of Resurrection with an eye of mercy, nor will He purify them from the filth of sins and disbelief. For them is a painful punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 78:

Indeed, among the Jews there is a group who distort speech from its places and alter the words of Allah, so that they may deceive others into thinking that this is from the revealed Scripture, namely the Torah, when it is not part of it at all. They say: "This is from Allah, Allah revealed it to His prophet Musa," but it is not from Allah. They say falsehood about Allah for the sake of their worldly gain, while they know that they are liars.

It is not fitting for any human being to whom Allah has given the Book, judgment, and prophethood, that he should then say to the people, "Worship me instead of Allah." Rather, (he would say), "Be people who are wise, learned in religion, and knowledgeable, through what you have been teaching others of the revelation of Allah the Exalted, and through what you study of it, by memorization, knowledge, and understanding."

It is not for any human being that he should command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords, worshipping them besides Allah. Would it be reasonable, O people, that he would command you to disbelieve in Allah after you have submitted to his command?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 81:

Mention, O Messenger, when God, glorified is He, took the firm covenant from all the prophets: ﴿Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must support him.﴾ Then He said: ﴿Do you acknowledge and accept this, and take upon that My binding covenant?﴾ They said: ﴿We acknowledge it.﴾ He said: ﴿Then let some of you bear witness against others, and bear witness against your nations concerning this. And I am with you among the witnesses.﴾ In this is the proof that God took the covenant from every prophet that he must believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), and God took the covenant from the nations of the prophets to do likewise.

Whoever turns away from the call of Islam after this clarification and this covenant which God took from His prophets, those are the ones who have left the religion of God and the obedience owed to their Lord.

Does it seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned?

Is it, then, other than the religion of Allah (that they desire) — that is, Islam, with which Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) — while to Him submits everyone in the heavens and the earth, willingly, as do the believers, and unwillingly at times of hardship, when that will not benefit them, as is the case with the disbelievers, just as all created beings submit to Him, and to Him they will be returned on the Day of Resurrection, where He will recompense each one for his deeds. This is a warning from Allah, exalted is He, to His creation that none of them should return to Him following any religion other than Islam.

Say, [O Messenger]: "We believe in God and have submitted to Him. There is no lord for us other than Him, and no deity worthy of worship for us besides Him. We believe in the revelation that God sent down to us, and that which He sent down to Abraham, the Friend of God (Khalil Allah), and to his two sons Ishmael and Isaac, and to Isaac's son Jacob son of Isaac, and that which He sent down to the Tribes (al-Asbat) — they are the prophets from the descendants of Jacob, who were among the twelve tribes of the Children of Israel — and what was given to Moses and Jesus of the Torah and the Gospel, and what God sent down to His prophets. We believe in all of that, and we make no distinction between any of them. And we, to God alone, are submissive in obedience, acknowledging to Him lordship, divinity, and worship."

And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, which is submission to God through monotheism and compliance with Him through obedience and worship, and [submission] to His Messenger, the seal of the prophets, Muhammad (ﷺ), through belief in him, following him, and loving him outwardly and inwardly, that will not be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers, who have diminished their souls' portions.

How will Allah guide to faith in Him and His Messenger a people who denied the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ after having believed in him, and who testified that Muhammad ﷺ is true and that what he brought is the truth, and clear proofs had come to them from Allah confirming that? Allah does not guide to the truth and rightness the wrongdoing people, namely those who turned away from the truth to falsehood, so they chose disbelief over faith.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 87:

Those are the wrongdoers. Their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together. So they are cast away from the mercy of Allah.
Remaining in the Fire, the punishment will not be lightened for them even briefly so that they may rest, nor will it be deferred to give them any excuse by which they might plead.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, the "Simplified Tafsir") on surah 3, verse 89:**

﴿Except for those who afterward repent and return to their Lord with sincere repentance, after their disbelief and wrongdoing, and who set right what they had corrupted by their repentance. Indeed, Allah accepts it, for He is Oft-Forgiving to the sins of His servants and Most Merciful to them.﴾

Those who disbelieve after their belief and persist in disbelief until death, their repentance will not be accepted when death comes; and those are the ones who have gone astray from the path, having missed its way.

Indeed, those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and died in disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, no one of them will be accepted on the Day of Resurrection even if he offered the whole earth filled with gold, to ransom himself from the punishment of Allah, and even if he actually offered it to ransom himself. For them is a painful punishment, and they will have no one to rescue them from the punishment of Allah.
You will never attain Paradise until you spend from what you love. Whatever you give in charity, whether little or much, God knows it well, and He will repay every spender according to his deeds.

All the good foods were lawful for the children of Ya'qub (peace be upon him), except what Ya'qub had forbidden to himself because of an illness that had afflicted him, and that was before the Torah was revealed. When the Torah was revealed, Allah forbade to the Children of Israel some of the foods that had been lawful for them, as a consequence of their wrongdoing and their transgression. Say to them, O Messenger: "Bring the Torah and recite what is in it, if you are truthful in your claim that Allah revealed in it the prohibition of what Ya'qub forbade to himself," so that you may know the truth of what came in the Qur'an, that Allah had not forbidden anything to the Children of Israel before the revelation of the Torah, except what Ya'qub had forbidden to himself.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 94:

Then whoever fabricates lies against Allah after the reading of the Torah and the clarity of the truth, those are the wrongdoers who attribute falsehood to Allah.

Say, [O Messenger], "Allah has spoken the truth in what He has reported and in what He has legislated. So if you are truthful in your love for and your affiliation with the Friend of Allah, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), then follow his religion (millah), which Allah has prescribed through the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ), for it is the truth about which there is no doubt. And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was not one of those who associate partners with Allah in His Oneness and in His worship, [not] in any way."

Indeed, the first house built for the worship of God on earth is the Sacred House of God that is in "Makkah." This House is blessed: good deeds are multiplied in it, mercies descend upon it, and in facing it during prayer and in making it one's destination for the Hajj and the 'Umrah there is goodness and guidance for all of mankind.

In this House there are clear signs that it is the building of Ibrahim, and that Allah has exalted and honoured it. Among them: the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), which is the stone on which he stood while he was raising the foundations of the House, together with his son Isma'il. Whoever enters this House is secure for himself, so that no one may harm him. Allah has made the Hajj (pilgrimage) obligatory upon every able person among the people, wherever he may be, to intend this House to perform the rites of Hajj (manasik). Whoever denies the obligation of Hajj has disbelieved, while Allah is free of need of it, of its performance, of his deeds, and of all His creation.

Say, [O Messenger], to the People of the Book, Jews and Christians: "Why do you deny the proofs of God, which indicate that the religion of God is Islam, and reject what is in your scriptures of evidence and proofs for that, while you know [it to be true]? And God is Witness over your deeds." In this there is a threat and a warning for them.

Say, O Messenger, to the Jews and Christians: Why do you bar from Islam those who wish to enter it, seeking to make it crooked and to turn it away from the right course and uprightness, while you yourselves know that what I have brought is the truth? And Allah is not unaware of what you do, and He will recompense you for that.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: if you obey a group of the Jews and the Christians, those who were given the Torah and the Gospel, they will lead you astray and cast doubts upon you regarding your religion, so that you revert to denying the truth after you had believed in it. Therefore, do not trust them with your religion, and do not accept from them any opinion or counsel.

How can you disbelieve in God, O believers, when the verses of the Qur'an are being recited to you and the Messenger of God, Muhammad (ﷺ), is among you, conveying them to you? Whoever relies upon God and holds fast to the Qur'an and the Sunnah (the Prophet's teachings, deeds and approvals) has been granted success in a clear path and a straight way.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law, fear Allah with the fear that is due to Him: that is, that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, thanked and not denied, remembered and not forgotten; and persist in holding fast to your Islam until the end of your lives, so that you meet Allah while you are upon it.

Hold fast all together to the Book of your Lord and the guidance of your Prophet, and do not do anything that leads to your division. Remember a great blessing with which Allah has favoured you: when you were, O believers, enemies before Islam, Allah joined your hearts in His love and the love of His Messenger, and placed in your hearts love for one another, so that by His bounty you became brothers loving one another. You were on the brink of the Fire of Hell, and Allah guided you to Islam and saved you from the Fire. Just as Allah has made clear to you the landmarks of true faith, so He makes clear to you everything that is good for you, so that you may be guided to the path of right conduct, follow it, and not go astray from it.

And let there be among you, O believers, a community that calls to good, enjoins what is right (al-ma'ruf), which is what is known to be good by the Sharia and by reason, and forbids what is wrong (al-munkar), which is what is known to be ugly by the Sharia and by reason. And those are the successful ones, who will attain the Gardens of Bliss.

"And do not be like the People of the Book, who fell into enmity and hatred among themselves, so that they split into sects and factions and differed concerning the foundations of their religion after the truth had become clear to them. Those [people] deserve a great and painful punishment."

On the Day of Resurrection, the faces of the people of happiness who believed in Allah and His Messenger and carried out His command will turn bright, while the faces of the people of wretchedness who denied His Messenger and disobeyed His command will turn dark. As for those whose faces have turned dark, it will be said to them as a rebuke: "Did you disbelieve after your belief, choosing disbelief over faith? So taste the punishment because of your disbelief."

And as for those whose faces turn white, with the radiance of bliss and with what they were given good tidings of, they are in Allah's Paradise and its bliss, and they will remain in it forever, never to leave it.

These are the verses of Allah and His clear proofs. We recite them to you, O Messenger, with truth and certainty. Allah does not wrong any of His creatures, nor does He diminish anything of their deeds, because He is the Just Judge who does not act unjustly.

This passage is from the commentary of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the King Fahd Complex commentary) on Surah Al-Imran, verse 109.

And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. It is His dominion alone, in creation and in management, and the return of all creatures is to Him alone, so He will recompense each one according to what it deserves.

You, O Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), are the best of nations and the most beneficial of people to mankind. You enjoin what is good (al-ma'ruf), which is that whose goodness is recognised by the Law (shar'an) and by reason ('aqlan), and you forbid what is evil (al-munkar), which is that whose ugliness is recognised by the Law and by reason, and you believe in Allah with a firm belief that is confirmed by action. Had the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, believed in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what was brought to them from Allah as you have believed, it would have been better for them in this world and in the Hereafter. Among them are believers who affirm the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) and act upon it, but they are few, and most of them are those who have departed from the religion of Allah and His obedience.

It will not harm you, these defiantly disobedient People of the Scripture, except for some hurt to your ears from words of polytheism, disbelief and the like. And if they fight you, they will be defeated, turning and fleeing with their backs to you; then they will not be helped against you in any way.

God has decreed that humiliation and abasement cling to the Jews as an inseparable condition; they are abased and held in contempt wherever they are found, except under a covenant from God and a covenant from people by which they are secured in their lives and property. That covenant is the contract of protection (dhimmah) for them, obligating them to abide by the rulings of Islam. They returned bearing wrath from God, deserving it, and humiliation and wretchedness were struck upon them. You will never see a Jew except that fear and terror of the people of faith are upon him. This is what God has imposed upon them because of their disbelief in God, their transgression of His limits, and their killing of the prophets unjustly and aggressively. Nothing emboldened them to this except their committing of sins and their transgressing the limits of God.

The Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 3, verse 113:

Not all of the People of the Book are alike. Among them is a upright community that adheres to the command of Allah, believes in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), stands in prayer through the night, reciting the verses of the Noble Qur'an in measured tones, and devoting themselves to communing with Allah in their prayers.
They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin all that is good, forbid all that is evil, and hasten to do good deeds. Those are among the righteous servants of Allah.

And whatever good deed they do, whether small or great, will not be lost with Allah; rather, it will be acknowledged for them and they will be rewarded for it. And Allah is All-Knowing of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) who do good deeds and keep away from what is forbidden, seeking the pleasure of Allah and desiring His reward.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 116:

Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and deny His messengers, their wealth and their children will not avail them anything against the punishment of Allah, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. And those are the companions of the Fire, abiding in it forever; they will never leave it.

The likeness of what the disbelievers spend in charity in this worldly life, and what they hope for in reward, is like a wind in which is severe cold, which blew upon the crop of a people who were hoping for its yield, and because of their sins the wind left nothing of it. And these disbelievers will find no reward in the Hereafter. God did not wrong them in that; rather, they wronged themselves by their disbelief and disobedience.

O you who have believed God and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not take the disbelievers as intimate friends (awliya') in place of the believers, disclosing your secrets to them. These people do not cease in their corruption of your affairs, and they rejoice at whatever harm and hardship befalls you. Hatred has already appeared in their speech, and what their breasts conceal of enmity toward you is greater and more severe. We have indeed made clear to you the proofs and arguments, so that you may take heed and be wary, if you are people who understand God's admonitions, His commands and His prohibitions.

Here is the proof of your error in loving them: you love them and do good to them, while they do not love you and harbor enmity and hatred toward you. You believe in all the revealed Books, including their Book, but they do not believe in your Book. So how can you love them?

"And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe'" (hypocritically). "But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage." That is, when they are alone with one another, grief and sorrow appear upon them, and they bite the tips of their fingers out of intense anger, because of what they see of the unity of the Muslims, the harmony of their word, the honoring of Islam, and the humbling of them through it.

Say to them, O Messenger: "Die in your rage." Indeed, Allah is aware of what the chests conceal, and He will recompense each soul for what it has put forward of good or evil.

Among the hostility of these people is that when something good befalls you, believers, such as victory or spoils of war, it distresses them and grief appears on them; but when something adverse strikes you, such as defeat or loss of wealth, lives and crops, they rejoice at it. Yet if you are patient over what has befallen you, and you fear Allah in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, their scheming will not harm you at all. Allah encompasses all that these disbelievers do of corruption, and He will requite them for it.

Remember, O Messenger, when you went out from your household in the morning, dressed for battle, arranging the ranks of your Companions and assigning each of them to his position, to meet the polytheists at the Battle of Uhud. And Allah is All-Hearing of your words, All-Knowing of your deeds.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 3:122 from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the "Simplified Commentary") of the King Fahd Complex:

Remember, O Prophet, when two groups from among you, the Banu Salamah and the Banu Harithah, were inclined to turn back, out of fear of meeting the enemy, along with their chief, the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy. But Allah protected and preserved them, so they continued marching with you, relying upon Allah. And upon Allah alone let the believers rely.

And God had already helped you at Badr, O believers, against your enemies the polytheists, though you were few in number and poorly equipped. So fear God by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, so that perhaps you will be thankful to Him for His blessings.

Recall, O Prophet, the situation of your companions at Badr, when it was difficult for them that reinforcements should come to the polytheists. So We revealed to you that you should say to them: "Would it not suffice you that your Lord aids you by sending down to you three thousand angels, sent down from the heaven to the battlefield, who will strengthen you and fight alongside you?"

Indeed, this reinforcement will suffice for you. And here is another good tiding for you: if you are patient in facing the enemy and fear Allah by doing what He has commanded you and avoiding what He has forbidden you, and the disbelievers of Makkah come upon you immediately, rushing to fight you, thinking that they will utterly destroy you, then Allah will reinforce you with five thousand angels, ﴿marked﴾, i.e., they had marked themselves and their horses with clear signs.

This is the commentary on Q. 3:126, from the tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex). Translating the passage:

And Allah did not make this reinforcement by the angels except as glad tidings for you, to give you good news by it, and so that your hearts may be reassured and find comfort in the promise of Allah to you. And victory is only from Allah, the Mighty, who cannot be overcome, the Wise in His management and His action.

And Allah's help was for you at Badr, so that He might destroy a group of the disbelievers by slaying them. Whoever of them escaped being killed returned grieved, his soul constricted, with disgrace and shame showing upon him.

This is the commentary of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the "Simplified Tafsir" of the King Fahd Complex) on surah 3, verse 128:

You have no part, O Messenger, in the affairs of the servants; rather, the entire matter belongs to Allah alone, with no partner. Perhaps some of those who fought against you will have their hearts opened to Islam and embrace it, and then Allah will accept their repentance. As for whoever remains upon his disbelief, Allah will punish him in this world and in the Hereafter, because of his wrongdoing and transgression.

To God alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills of His servants by His mercy, and He punishes whom He wills by His justice. And God is Oft-Forgiving to the sins of His servants, Most Merciful to them.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted in accordance with His law, beware of riba (usury, interest) in all its forms. Do not take, in lending, any increase over your principal, even if it is small. How much more so when this increase keeps multiplying every time the term for repaying the debt comes due? And fear Allah by adhering to His law, so that you may be successful in this world and the Hereafter.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 3, verse 131:**

﴿And make for yourselves a shield between yourselves and the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.﴾

And obey Allah, O believers, in what He has commanded you of acts of obedience and in what He has forbidden you of consuming usury and other things. And obey the Messenger, so that you may be shown mercy, and not be punished.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 133:**

Hasten to obey Allah and His Messenger so that you may obtain a great forgiveness from your Lord and a vast Paradise, whose breadth is like the heavens and the earth, which Allah has prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun).

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 134:

Those who spend their wealth in ease and in hardship, and those who restrain their anger and pardon people. When they are able to retaliate, they forgive those who wronged them. This is the excellence (ihsan) that Allah loves its people for.

Those who, when they commit a grave sin or wrong themselves by committing something less than that, remember God's promise and His threat, so they turn to their Lord in repentance, asking Him to forgive their sins, and they are certain that none forgives sins except God. Therefore they do not persist in disobedience, and they know that if they repent, God will accept their repentance.

These are the ones described with those great qualities: their reward is that Allah will cover over their sins, and for them are gardens beneath which rivers of sweet water flow, through their trees and mansions, abiding therein forever, never to leave them. And excellent is the reward of those who act: forgiveness and Paradise.

God addresses the believers, when they were afflicted on the day of Uhud, consoling them: nations have passed away before you, and the believers among them were tested by fighting the disbelievers, yet the final outcome was theirs. So travel through the earth, taking warning from what became of those who denied Allah and His messengers.

This Qur'an is a clarification and a guidance to the path of truth, and a reminder before which the hearts of the God-conscious (al-muttaqun) humble themselves, namely those who fear Allah. They were singled out for this because they are the ones who benefit from it, to the exclusion of others.

Do not weaken, O believers, in fighting your enemy, and do not grieve over what has befallen you at Uhud; you will be the victors, and the final outcome will be yours, if you are truly believers in God and His Messenger, following His law.

If you (believers) have suffered wounds or death in the battle of Uhud, then grieve not: the disbelievers suffered wounds and death like that in the battle of Badr. These days We alternate among people: victory one time, defeat another. This is because of the wisdom in that, so that what Allah knew from eternity becomes manifest, so that Allah may distinguish the true believer from others, and so that He may honour some of you with martyrdom. And Allah does not love those who wrong themselves and who held back from fighting in His cause.
This defeat that befell the Muslims at Uhud was a test and a purification for the believers, a means of separating them from the hypocrites, and a destruction for the disbelievers.

O Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), did you think you would enter Paradise without being tested by fighting and hardships? You will not attain entry into it until you are tested, and Allah will make manifest, so that His creation can see it, the knowledge of those among you who strive in His cause and who are patient in confronting the enemies.

This is a translation of the commentary on Qur'an 3:143, which is part of the passage you provided.

And indeed you used to wish for the encounter with the enemy before the battle of Uhud, O believers, so that you might attain the honour of jihad and martyrdom in the way of God, which your brothers had been granted in the battle of Badr. Now here it is: what you wished for and sought has come to you. So take your place and fight, and be steadfast.

Muhammad ﷺ is only a messenger, and messengers came before him. ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; [other] messengers have passed away before him.﴾ He conveys the message of his Lord. So if he dies when his term is complete, or is killed, as the enemies spread the rumour, will you turn back on your religion and abandon what your Prophet brought you? Whoever turns back on his religion will not harm Allah at all; he only harms himself, a great harm. As for those who remain steadfast in faith and give thanks to their Lord for the blessing of Islam, Allah will reward them with the best of rewards.

No soul can die except by the permission of Allah and His decree, and only when it has fulfilled the term that Allah has appointed for it. Allah has ordained that term as a fixed writ, which can neither be brought forward nor postponed. As for the one who seeks by his deeds the goods of this world, We shall give him what We have apportioned for him of provision, but he will have no share in the Hereafter. And the one who seeks by his deeds the reward from Allah in the Hereafter, We shall grant him what he sought, and give him his reward in full, along with what has been apportioned for him of provision in this world. Such a person has been thankful to Us through his obedience and his striving, and We shall reward the thankful with goodness.

Many of the earlier prophets fought in battle alongside large throngs of their companions, yet they did not weaken because of the wounds or deaths that befell them, for it was in the cause of their Lord. Nor did they falter, nor did they submit to their enemy; rather, they were patient in the face of what afflicted them. And Allah loves those who are patient.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 147:

Their only words were: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people.﴾ That is, the words of these steadfast ones were nothing but a supplication: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins, and the transgressions we committed in the matter of our religion; make our feet firm so that we do not flee from fighting our enemy; and grant us victory over those who denied Your oneness and the prophethood of Your messengers."

Then Allah gave those who were patient their reward in this world, by granting them victory over their enemies and establishing them firmly in the land, and with the excellent, great reward in the Hereafter, which is the Gardens of Bliss. And Allah loves everyone who excels in his worship of his Lord and in his dealings with His creation.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law: if you obey those who denied My divinity and did not believe in My messengers, from among the Jews, the Christians, the hypocrites and the polytheists, in what they command you and forbid you, they will lead you astray from the path of truth, and you will turn back from your religion, and so you will return to manifest loss and certain destruction.

The commentary on Surah 3, verse 150:

"They will not give you victory; rather, Allah is your Helper, and He is the best of helpers, so there is no need for anyone's support alongside Him."

We will cast terror and dread into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they associated with Allah deities that were falsely claimed, for which they have no proof or evidence that they deserve to be worshipped alongside Allah. Their state in this world is terror and panic before the believers. As for their place in the Hereafter, to which they will return, it is the Fire; this is because of their wrongdoing and transgression. Wretched is this abode as a place for them.

Allah had indeed fulfilled His promise of victory to you when you were killing the disbelievers at the Battle of Uhud, by His permission. But then you lost heart, grew weak in fighting, and disputed among yourselves: should you remain at your positions or leave them to collect the spoils alongside those who were gathering them? You disobeyed the command of your Messenger when he ordered you not to leave your positions under any circumstances. Defeat befell you after He had shown you what you love, namely victory. It became clear that among you were those who desired the spoils, and among you were those who desired the Hereafter and its reward. Then He turned your faces away from your enemy in order to test you. Allah knew your regret and repentance, so He pardoned you, and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.

Remember, O companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), what happened to you when you were climbing the mountain in flight from your enemies, not turning your heads toward anyone, because of the bewilderment, fear, and terror that had overtaken you, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood firm on the battlefield calling out to you from behind you: "Come to me, servants of Allah!" But you neither heard nor looked. So Allah repaid you with distress and hardship and grief, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you of victory and spoils, nor over what had befallen you of fear and defeat. And Allah is All-Aware of all your deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him.

Then, by the mercy of God toward the sincere believers, He cast into their hearts—after the distress and grief that had befallen them—tranquility and trust in God's promise. Its effect was a drowsiness that overcame a group among them, namely the people of sincerity and certainty. Another group, however, were concerned only with saving themselves; their resolve weakened, they busied themselves with their own selves, and they harbored ill thoughts about their Lord, His religion, and His Prophet. They supposed that God would not complete the affair of His Messenger, and that Islam would never stand firm. For this reason you see them regretful of their departure, saying to one another: "Did we have any choice in going out to fight?" Say to them, O Messenger: "Indeed, the whole matter belongs to God; it is He who decreed your departure and what befell you." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you, of regret over their going out to fight, saying: "If we had had any choice at all, we would not have been killed here." Say to them: "The terms of death are in the hand of God. Even if you had been in your houses, and God had decreed that you would die, those whom God had written death for would have gone forth to the places where they would be killed. God did not do this except to test what is in your breasts of doubt and hypocrisy, and to distinguish the wicked from the good, and to make manifest to the people the state of the believer from the hypocrite in words and deeds. God is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts of His creatures; nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him."

Indeed, those of you who turned their backs (fled) on the day the two armies met, [that is,] the believers and the polytheists, at the Battle of Uhud—O Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ)—it was only Satan who caused them to slip into this sin, because of some of the sins they had committed. But Allah has already pardoned them and did not punish them. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving to those who sin and repent, Forbearing, who does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not be like the disbelievers who do not believe in their Lord. They say to their brethren from among the people of disbelief, when they set out travelling through the land of Allah seeking their livelihood, or when they were with the raiders and fighters and then died or were killed: "Had they not gone out and not fought, and had they stayed with us, they would not have died and would not have been killed." This saying only increases them in pain, grief and regret that settles in their hearts. As for the believers, they know that this is by the decree of Allah, so Allah guides their hearts and eases the calamity for them. Allah gives life to whom He has decreed life, even if he is traveling or fighting in battle, and causes to die whose term has ended, even if he is residing at home. Allah is All-Seeing of whatever you do, and He will recompense you for it.

If you are killed, O believers, while striving in the way of Allah, or you die during the fighting, then Allah will surely forgive you your sins and have mercy upon you with a mercy from Him, and you will attain the Gardens of Bliss. And that is better than this world and all that its people gather.

And if your lifespans come to an end in this worldly life, and you die on your beds, or you are killed on the battlefield, you will surely be gathered to God alone, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 3, verse 159:

By a mercy from Allah, [you were gentle] with them, O Prophet. Allah bestowed His favor upon you, so you were gentle with them. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, your companions would have dispersed from around you. So do not hold them to account for what they did at the Battle of Uhud, and ask Allah, O Prophet, to forgive them. Consult them on matters that require consultation. Then, when you have resolved upon a matter after consultation, carry it out, relying upon Allah alone. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 3, verse 160:**

If Allah supports you with His victory and aid, no one can overcome you. But if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after His forsaking you? So let the believers put their trust in Allah alone.

It is not for any prophet to betray his companions by taking anything from the spoils beyond what Allah has allotted to him. Whoever among you does that will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying what he took; he will be disgraced thereby before the assembled gathering. Then every soul will be paid in full for what it earned, without any reduction and without injustice.
Those whose aim is the pleasure of Allah are not equal to those who are absorbed in sins and displease their Lord, and who thereby deserve to dwell in Hell, and how evil a destination it is.

The people of Paradise, who follow what pleases God, differ in their ranks, and the people of the Fire, who follow what angers God, differ in their levels of punishment. They are not equal. God is All-Seeing of their deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him.

Certainly God bestowed His favor upon the believers among the Arabs, when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them the verses of the Qur'an, purifying them from polytheism and corrupt morals, and teaching them the Qur'an and the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition). Before this Messenger, they were indeed in manifest error and ignorance.

Or when a calamity struck you—O believers—and it was what had befallen you on the day of Uhud, when you had already inflicted twice as much on the polytheists on the day of Badr, you said in astonishment: "How can this be, when we are Muslims and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is among us, and these are polytheists?" Say to them, O Prophet: "This calamity that has struck you is from your own selves; it is because of your disobedience to the command of your Messenger and your turning to gather the spoils of war. Indeed, God does what He wills and decrees what He desires, and none can avert His judgment."

Whatever harm befell you, of wounds or deaths, at the Battle of Uhud on the day when the two hosts met, the host of the believers and the host of the polytheists, was by the decree and destiny of Allah. Victory was first for the believers, and then it went to the polytheists. All of this happened so that what Allah had known from eternity might become manifest, and so that He might distinguish the sincere believers from among you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 167:

And so that He would make known the hypocrites, those whom Allah has exposed for what is in their hearts, when the believers said to them, "Come, fight alongside us in the way of Allah, or at least be a support to us by increasing our numbers." They said, "If we knew that you were going to fight, we would certainly have followed you." They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, for they say with their mouths what is not in their hearts. And Allah knows best what they conceal in their breasts.

These hypocrites are the ones who stayed behind and said of their brothers who were killed while fighting alongside the Muslims against the polytheists on the day of Uhud: "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say to them, O Messenger: "Then ward off death from yourselves, if you are truthful in your claim that, had they obeyed you, they would not have been killed, and that you yourselves have escaped it by staying away from the fighting."

Do not think, O Prophet, that those who were killed in the cause of Allah are dead. Rather, they are alive, in a barzakh life (the intermediate state between death and resurrection), in the presence of their Lord, for whose sake they struggled and died in His cause. Their provision flows to them in Paradise, and they are made to enjoy its bounties.

The commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 170:

Happiness has truly overtaken them when Allah bestowed His favour upon them. Out of His great generosity and vast bounty, He gave them such blessings and contentment that their eyes are delighted. They rejoice over their brothers, the fighters in the way of Allah, whom they left behind while still alive, so that those brothers might attain the same success they attained. They know that they will receive the same good they have received, if those brothers are martyred in the way of Allah, sincerely devoted to Him, and that there is no fear upon them regarding what lies ahead of them of the matters of the Hereafter, nor will they grieve over what they missed of the portions of this worldly life.

They rejoice greatly in what they have been given of Allah's blessings and abundant bounty, and [they rejoice] that Allah does not waste the reward of those who believe in Him; rather, He multiplies it and increases it from His bounty.

Those who answered the call of Allah and His Messenger and went out in pursuit of the polytheists to Ḥamrā' al-Asad after their defeat at the Battle of Uhud, despite the pains and wounds they had suffered, and who exerted their utmost effort and adhered to the guidance of their Prophet—for those among them who did good and were God-conscious, there is a great reward.

And they are those to whom some of the polytheists said: "Indeed, Abu Sufyan and those with him have resolved to return to you to annihilate you, so beware of them and avoid facing them, for you have no strength against them." But this warning only increased them in certainty and in belief in Allah's promise to them, and it did not turn them away from their resolve. So they set out to wherever Allah willed, and they said: "Allah is sufficient for us" (ḥasbunā Allāh), meaning: He is our Protector, "and He is the best Disposer of affairs" (wa-niʿma al-wakīl), the One to whom the management of His servants' affairs is entrusted.

They returned from Hamra' al-Asad to Madinah with a blessing from Allah, a great reward, and with His bounty, a high station. They had increased in faith and certainty, they humiliated the enemies of Allah, and they succeeded in being safe from being killed and from fighting. And they pursued the pleasure of Allah by their obedience to Him and to His Messenger. Allah is the Possessor of kindness and abundant giving, vast toward them and toward others.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 175:

It is only Satan who frightens you with his allies. So do not fear them (the disbelievers), but fear Me by turning wholeheartedly to My obedience, if you are truly believers in Me and followers of My Messenger.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 176:

Let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you, O Messenger. By their hastening into denial and error, they will not harm Allah in the least. They only harm themselves, by depriving themselves of the sweetness of faith and of great reward. Allah wills that He give them no share of reward in the Hereafter, because they turned away from the call to the truth. For them is a severe punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 177:

Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith will not harm Allah at all. Rather, the harm of their deed returns to themselves, and for them in the Hereafter is painful punishment.
And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for themselves. We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 179:
