God would not leave you, O believers in God and His Messenger, who act according to His law, in the state you are in, with the believer among you mixed up with the hypocrite, until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, so that the hypocrite is recognized from the true believer. It is not part of God's wisdom to let you, O believers, know the unseen that He knows about His servants, so that you could recognize the believer from the hypocrite among them. Rather, He distinguishes them through trials and tests. However, God, may He be exalted, chooses from among His messengers whomever He wills, in order to inform him of some of the knowledge of the unseen through revelation from Him. So believe in God and His Messenger. If you believe with sincere faith and fear your Lord by obeying Him, then you will have a great reward with God.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 180:

Let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty suppose that this stinginess is good for them. Rather, it is evil for them, because the wealth they have hoarded will become a collar of fire placed around their necks on the Day of Resurrection. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is the Owner of all sovereignty, He is the Everlasting after all His creation has perished, and He is All-Aware of all your deeds, and He will recompense each according to the measure of what he deserves.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 181:

Allah has certainly heard the statement of those Jews who said: "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich." They ask us to lend Him wealth. We shall record what they have said, and we shall record that they are content with the killing of their forefathers of the prophets of Allah, wrongfully and aggressively. We will hold them accountable for that in the Hereafter, and We will say to them, while they are being tormented in the Fire: "Taste the punishment of the burning Fire."

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 3, Verse 182:**

That severe punishment is because of what you sent forward in your worldly life of acts of disobedience, whether spoken, physical, or doctrinal, and because Allah is not unjust to His servants.

These Jews, when they were invited to Islam, said: "God has commanded us in the Torah not to believe any messenger who comes to us claiming to be a messenger of God until he brings us a sacrifice (qurban) by which he draws near to God, and then a fire descends from heaven and consumes it." Say to them, O Messenger: "You are lying in what you say, for there came to your fathers messengers before me with the miracles and proofs of their truthfulness, and with what you have mentioned of bringing the offering that fire consumes. So why did your fathers kill those prophets, if you are truthful in your claim?"

If they deny you, O Messenger, then the Jews and others among the people of disbelief have denied you. Indeed, many messengers before you were denied by falsifiers. They came to their peoples with clear miracles, with compelling proofs, with the heavenly scriptures that are a light dispelling darknesses, and with the Book that is manifest and clear.

Every soul shall taste death, and by this all creation will return to their Lord so that He may call them to account. You will only be given your full reward for your deeds on the Day of Resurrection, complete and not diminished. Whoever is granted honor by his Lord, is saved from the Fire, and is admitted into Paradise has indeed attained the utmost of what he seeks. And the life of this world is nothing but fleeting enjoyment, so do not be deceived by it.

You will surely be tested, O believers, in your wealth and in yourselves: in your wealth through spending, both obligatory and recommended, and through the calamities that befall it; and in yourselves through the acts of obedience incumbent upon you, and through what befalls you of wounds, killing, and the loss of loved ones. This is so that the sincere believer may be distinguished from others.

And you will surely hear, from the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists, much that will hurt your ears: words of associationism and disparagement of your religion. But if you are patient, O believers, in all of that, and fear God by adhering to His obedience and avoiding His disobedience, then that is among the matters that are resolved upon and in which people should vie with one another.

Remember, O Messenger, when Allah took a binding covenant from those who were given the Scripture, from the Jews and the Christians: the Torah was for the Jews and the Injil for the Christians, so that they would act upon them, explain to the people what is in them, and not conceal that or hide it. But they abandoned the covenant and did not adhere to it, and they took a paltry price in exchange for their concealing the truth and their distorting the Book. Evil is what they bought, in their neglect of the covenant and their alteration of the Book.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 188:

Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done of ugly deeds, like the Jews, the hypocrites and others, and who love to be praised by people for what they did not do, are saved from the punishment of Allah in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is painful punishment. In the verse there is a severe warning for everyone who commits an evil deed and is pleased with it, and for everyone who boasts of what he did not do, so that people will praise him and commend him.
"To Allah alone belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and Allah is over all things capable."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 190:

Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth without any prior model, and in the alternation of night and day, and in their difference in length and shortness, there are great signs and proofs of God's oneness for people of sound intellect.

Those who remember Allah in all their circumstances: standing, sitting, and lying on their sides. And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, saying: "Our Lord, You did not create this creation in vain; You are exalted above that, so spare us the punishment of the Fire."

O our Lord, save us from the Fire. For You, O Allah, whoever You cause to enter the Fire because of his sins has indeed been disgraced and humiliated. And the wrongdoers, who wronged themselves, have no helper who can avert God's punishment from them on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 193:

"Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith, [saying]: 'Believe in your Lord,' so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our faults, and make us die among the righteous." (Qur'an 3:193)

Note: the Qur'anic quotation within this passage is translated above from the verse itself, as the passage in the commentary is a paraphrase of it. The commentary explains that the caller is your Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), who calls people to affirm belief in You, to acknowledge Your oneness, and to act upon Your law. So we responded to his call and affirmed his message. Forgive us our sins, conceal our faults, and join us with the righteous.

O our Lord, grant us what You promised us through the tongues of Your messengers of victory, empowerment, success and guidance, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection for our sins. Indeed, You are Generous; You do not fail to fulfill a promise You made to Your servants.

Allah answered their supplication by assuring them that He does not waste the effort of any of them who does righteous deeds, whether male or female. They are equal in brotherhood in the religion, in obedience, and in the acceptance of deeds. As for those who emigrated out of desire for the pleasure of Allah, were driven out of their homes, suffered harm for obeying their Lord and worshipping Him, and fought and were killed in the cause of Allah, to raise His word: Allah will surely cover over for them the sins they committed, just as He covered them in this world, so He will not call them to account for them; and He will surely admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, through their palaces and trees, as a reward from Allah. And with Allah is the best of rewards.

Do not be deceived, O Messenger, by the comfortable living and abundant provision enjoyed by those who disbelieve in Allah, nor by their movement from place to place for trade and the pursuit of profits and wealth. Before long, all of this will be taken away from them, and they will find themselves held captive by their evil deeds.

The verse: ﴿مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ ۖ ثُمَّ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ﴾ is the Qur'anic quotation in the earlier part of the commentary, but the passage given to translate is the commentary text itself.

Translation:

A small, fleeting enjoyment; then their final destination on the Day of Resurrection will be the Fire, and how wretched a resting place it is.

But those who feared their Lord, obeyed His commands, and avoided His prohibitions — for them Allah has prepared gardens beneath which rivers flow, through their palaces and trees. They will abide therein forever and will never leave it. What is with Allah is greater and better for the people of obedience than the comforts of this world in which the disbelievers revel.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 3, verse 199:

Indeed, among the People of the Book there are some who believe in Allah as the one Lord and the one God worthy of worship, and in what has been sent down to you (this Qur'an), and in what was sent down to them (the Torah and the Gospel), humbling themselves before Allah and submitting to Him. They do not sell the signs of Allah for a small price of the goods of this world, and they do not conceal what Allah has sent down, nor do they distort it, unlike others among the People of the Book. Those will have a great reward with their Lord on the day they meet Him, and He will pay them in full, without any reduction. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning. Nothing hinders Him from counting their deeds and calling them to account for them.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law: be patient in obedience to your Lord, and patient over what befalls you of harm and trial. Outdo your enemies in patience, so that they are not more steadfast than you, and remain steadfast in striving against His enemy and your enemy. Fear Allah in all your conditions, in the hope that you will succeed in attaining His pleasure in this world and the Hereafter.
